questions.question: For a hairdryer, a light bulb and a minibus taxi, name the input energy, the useful output and the wasted output.
questions.expected_answer: Hairdryer: input electrical; useful output heat and kinetic energy of moving air; wasted output sound. Light bulb: input electrical; useful output light; wasted output heat. Minibus taxi: input chemical potential energy in fuel; useful output kinetic energy; wasted output heat (engine, exhaust, brakes) and sound.

questions.question: Explain, using the law of conservation of energy, why the useful output of a machine is always less than its input. Use a light bulb receiving 100 J that gives out 10 J of light as an example.
questions.expected_answer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, so input energy equals useful output plus wasted output. Every real machine changes some input into unwanted forms, mainly heat and sound, because of friction, air resistance and electrical resistance, so the useful output must be less than the input. Bulb: 100 J in = 10 J light (useful) + 90 J heat (wasted).

questions.question: Describe four ways to reduce wasted energy and explain how each works.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: oil moving parts or use ball bearings (reduces friction so less kinetic energy becomes heat and sound); streamline vehicles (reduces air resistance); use LED bulbs and appliances with good energy labels (more efficient, less heat wasted); insulate geysers and pipes, put lids on pots (less heat lost to surroundings); switch appliances off at the wall (stops standby waste); keep tyres properly inflated (less rolling friction).
